# MCP tool reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/docs/reference.ts. Do not edit; run `pnpm docs:reference`. -->

RenderWeld offers **78 tools** at `/mcp`, generated here from the server's tool registry.
Every tool has a REST equivalent under `/v1` with the same scope. Tool names are **experimental until v1.0**.
Errors come back as a tool result with `isError: true` and `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details" } }`.

| Group | Tools |
| --- | --- |

| Media providers | `list_providers`, `configure_provider`, `run_provider`, `generate_voice` |
| Rendering and jobs | `preview_scene`, `render_project`, `get_job`, `list_jobs`, `get_job_logs`, `cancel_job`, `retry_job`, `get_render_output`, `get_frames`, `list_renders`, `get_analytics_summary` |
| Workspaces | `get_workspace`, `list_workspaces`, `create_workspace`, `update_workspace`, `delete_workspace`, `restore_workspace` |

## Start here

What this server can do, the manifest schema and the installed templates. Call these before anything else.

### `get_capabilities`

**Get server capabilities**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/capabilities`.

Start here. Returns what this RenderWeld server can do right now: installed engines (and whether each can render on this machine), templates, themes, media providers (configured or not, with cost notes), render backends, limits (fps, max duration, upload size) and tool versions. Never guess an engine, template or provider: use what this returns.

No arguments.

### `get_me`

**Get the calling API key**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/me`.

Returns the API key this call uses: id, name, scopes (read, write, render, admin), expiry, limits and its render usage today and this month. Never the secret. Use it to see what this key may do before calling a tool that needs another scope.

No arguments.

### `get_project_schema`

**Get the project manifest JSON Schema**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/schema/project`.

Returns the JSON Schema of the project manifest (current schemaVersion). Use it to write valid manifests. Cross-field rules (template props, durations, asset references) are checked by validate_project.

No arguments.

### `list_templates`

**List scene templates**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/templates`.

Lists scene templates with their engine, description, supported duration range in seconds, the theme tokens they read, and the JSON Schema of their props. A scene uses { engine, template, props }. The html engine also accepts raw { html, css } instead of a template.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `engine` | string | no | Only templates of this engine, e.g. "remotion". |

### `get_skill`

**Read a craft skill**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/skills`, `GET /v1/skills/:name`.

Rules for one step of making a video, with numbers, so the result follows professional craft, published standards and the physical world instead of generic defaults. Built in: video-brief (what to ask before assuming), script-timing (words and reading time in frames), layout-and-type (safe areas for every aspect ratio, type size, contrast), motion-design (easing, durations, springs), camera-language (shot sizes, moves, cuts), physical-plausibility (gravity, weight, walking, blinking, artefacts in generated footage), sound-and-mix (loudness, ducking, sound-effect timing), voice-over (pace, pronunciation, consent), captions-and-accessibility (caption limits, flashing), av-sync (tolerances, frame arithmetic, lip sync), brand-consistency and review-and-qa. The operator may add more (skills.dir). Without name: the list. With name: the skill as Markdown. Also the resources renderweld://skills/<name>.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | no | Skill name, e.g. "layout-and-type". Omit to list the skills. |

## Projects

A project is one manifest (v0.2). Every change is stored as a new version.

### `list_projects`

**List projects**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/projects`.

Lists projects on this server with title, version, scene count and duration (no manifests; get_project has the manifest). Returns one page, newest first: at most `limit` items (default 50, max 200) and `nextCursor`. When nextCursor is not null there are more: call again with the same arguments plus `cursor: nextCursor` until it is null. Without a cursor you get the first (newest) page only, not everything.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer | no | Page size: 1 to 200, default 50. |
| `cursor` | string | no | nextCursor from the previous page of this list (same filters), unchanged. Omit for the first page. |

### `create_project`

**Create a project**. Scope: `write`. REST: `POST /v1/projects`.

Creates a project from a manifest. Minimal manifest: { schemaVersion: "0.2", projectId, title, output: { width: 1080, height: 1920, fps: 30, format: "mp4" }, scenes: [{ id, engine, template, durationSeconds, props }] }. output can be any even size from 16 to 4096 px, e.g. 1920x1080 (16:9), 1080x1080 (1:1), 1080x1350 (4:5), 1080x1920 (9:16, the usual default) or 3840x2160 (4K); built-in templates lay themselves out for the aspect ratio and keep text inside the safe area. Optional: brief (brief.platform sets the safe area for app overlays), theme, audio, assets (scenes use them by id: template props media and logo, or asset:<id> in html), captions. The manifest is validated against installed engines and templates; on failure you get every problem with its path. v0.1 manifests are migrated automatically.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `manifest` | object | yes | A project manifest (schemaVersion "0.2"; "0.1" is migrated). Call get_project_schema for the full JSON Schema. |
| `idempotencyKey` | string | no | Optional idempotency key (e.g. a UUID you generate once per intended action): retrying the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result instead of doing it twice; the same key with different arguments fails with idempotency_conflict. Kept 24 h. |

### `get_project`

**Get a project**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/projects/:id`.

Returns the current manifest, its version number and the computed timing of every scene (start frame, duration in frames and seconds). Pass version to read an older saved version.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `version` | integer | no |  |

### `update_project`

**Update a project**. Scope: `write`. REST: `PATCH /v1/projects/:id`.

Changes a project. Give either patch (a JSON merge patch, RFC 7396: objects merge, null deletes a key, arrays replace) or manifest (a full replacement). Because null deletes, a patch cannot set a field to null: for caption style use "none" (captions.style.background "none" = no box, outline "none" = no outline); for other nullable fields send the full manifest. For single scenes prefer add_scene / update_scene. Every update is validated and saved as a new version.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `patch` | object | no | JSON merge patch, e.g. { "title": "New title", "brief": { "goal": "..." } }. |
| `manifest` | object | no | A project manifest (schemaVersion "0.2"; "0.1" is migrated). Call get_project_schema for the full JSON Schema. |
| `expectedVersion` | integer | no | Optional optimistic-concurrency check: the project version you last read. The call fails with version_conflict if it changed. |

### `validate_project`

**Validate a project**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `POST /v1/projects/:id/validate`.

Full validation report: errors (block rendering) and warnings (e.g. missing licence, rounding of durationSeconds, caption quality rules), plus a summary (scenes, total frames, duration, size, engines). Checks schema, template props and durations, theme, assets on disk, render backend and engine availability on this machine.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |

### `list_project_versions`

**List saved versions of a project**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/projects/:id/versions`.

Every update saves a new version. Returns the version numbers; read one with get_project { version }.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |

### `delete_project`

**Delete a project**. Scope: `write`, destructive. REST: `DELETE /v1/projects/:id`.

Deletes a project with all its versions and renders, and cancels its queued and running renders and previews. Cannot be undone; confirm with the user first.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |

## Scenes

Scenes play back to back. Every edit returns the timing of every scene.

### `add_scene`

**Add a scene**. Scope: `write`. REST: `POST /v1/projects/:id/scenes`.

Adds a scene at index (default: the end). Scene: { id, engine, template, props, durationSeconds \| durationFrames } or for the html engine { id, engine: "html", html, css, durationSeconds }. Scenes play back to back with hard cuts; timing is exact to the frame.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `scene` | object | yes | The scene object. |
| `index` | integer | no | Position (0 = first). |
| `expectedVersion` | integer | no | Optional optimistic-concurrency check: the project version you last read. The call fails with version_conflict if it changed. |
| `idempotencyKey` | string | no | Optional idempotency key (e.g. a UUID you generate once per intended action): retrying the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result instead of doing it twice; the same key with different arguments fails with idempotency_conflict. Kept 24 h. |

### `update_scene`

**Update a scene**. Scope: `write`. REST: `PATCH /v1/projects/:id/scenes/:sceneId`.

Changes one scene with a JSON merge patch, e.g. { "props": { "headline": "New" } } or { "durationSeconds": 4 }. Setting durationSeconds replaces durationFrames (and vice versa); setting template replaces html/css.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `sceneId` | string | yes |  |
| `patch` | object | yes |  |
| `expectedVersion` | integer | no | Optional optimistic-concurrency check: the project version you last read. The call fails with version_conflict if it changed. |

### `remove_scene`

**Remove a scene**. Scope: `write`, destructive. REST: `DELETE /v1/projects/:id/scenes/:sceneId`.

Removes one scene (a project keeps at least one). Earlier versions stay readable with get_project { version }.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `sceneId` | string | yes |  |
| `expectedVersion` | integer | no | Optional optimistic-concurrency check: the project version you last read. The call fails with version_conflict if it changed. |

### `reorder_scenes`

**Reorder scenes**. Scope: `write`, idempotent. REST: `POST /v1/projects/:id/scenes:reorder`.

Sets the scene order. order must list every scene id exactly once.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `order` | string[] | yes |  |
| `expectedVersion` | integer | no | Optional optimistic-concurrency check: the project version you last read. The call fails with version_conflict if it changed. |

## Themes

Colours, fonts and motion speed that every template reads.

### `list_themes`

**List themes**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/themes`.

Lists brand themes (built-in "default" and "midnight" plus custom ones) with their tokens: colours, font family, heading weight, motion speed, caption style.

No arguments.

### `get_theme`

**Get a theme**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/themes/:id`.

Returns one theme (built-in or custom) with all its tokens: colours, font, weights, motion speed, caption style.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `themeId` | string | yes |  |

### `create_theme`

**Create a theme**. Scope: `write`. REST: `POST /v1/themes`.

Creates a reusable brand theme. tokens needs colors {background, surface, text, mutedText, accent, accent2} as #rrggbb and fontFamily (a CSS font-family list); optional headingWeight (100-900), radius, spacing, motionSpeed (0.25-4), captionStyle. Apply it with set_theme.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Lowercase id, e.g. "acme". |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `description` | string | no |  |
| `tokens` | object | yes |  |
| `idempotencyKey` | string | no | Optional idempotency key (e.g. a UUID you generate once per intended action): retrying the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result instead of doing it twice; the same key with different arguments fails with idempotency_conflict. Kept 24 h. |

### `update_theme`

**Replace a custom theme**. Scope: `write`, idempotent. REST: `PUT /v1/themes/:id`.

Replaces a custom theme (built-in themes cannot be changed). Same fields as create_theme.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `themeId` | string | yes |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `description` | string | no |  |
| `tokens` | object | yes |  |

### `delete_theme`

**Delete a custom theme**. Scope: `write`, destructive. REST: `DELETE /v1/themes/:id`.

Deletes a custom theme. Projects that use it fail validation until they pick another theme.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `themeId` | string | yes |  |

### `set_theme`

**Set the project theme**. Scope: `write`, idempotent. REST: `PUT /v1/projects/:id/theme`.

Sets the theme: a theme id (see list_themes) or inline tokens on top of a base theme, e.g. { "base": "midnight", "tokens": { "colors": { "accent": "#ff8800" } } }. Scene props such as accent/background still override per scene.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `theme` | string \| object | yes |  |
| `expectedVersion` | integer | no | Optional optimistic-concurrency check: the project version you last read. The call fails with version_conflict if it changed. |

## Assets and audio

Music, voice, sound effects, images and fonts, with licence metadata.

### `add_asset_from_url`

**Import an asset from a URL**. Scope: `write`. REST: `POST /v1/assets`.

Downloads an image, audio, video or font from a public https URL into the server asset store (size-limited, private networks refused, type checked from the bytes) and, with projectId, adds it to the project as assetId. Only use files you have the rights to; pass license metadata. Use it in scenes by its manifest id: template props media: { asset, fit: cover\|contain\|blur-fill, start (video in-point, s), dim } and logo: { asset, corner, size }, or asset:<id> in html scenes (<img src="asset:logo">, <video src="asset:clip">, url(asset:hero)). Video is frame-accurate at any frame rate; SVG is stored sanitised (no scripts, handlers or remote references). A font is used by naming its family (metadata.font.family) in the theme fontFamily; Inter, Source Serif 4 and JetBrains Mono are bundled. With projectId the asset belongs to that project; without, every project of the workspace may use it.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | yes |  |
| `projectId` | string | no | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `assetId` | string | no | Id to use in the manifest, e.g. "music". |
| `license` | object | no | Licence metadata for the asset (recommended; missing licences produce a warning). |
| `idempotencyKey` | string | no | Optional idempotency key (e.g. a UUID you generate once per intended action): retrying the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result instead of doing it twice; the same key with different arguments fails with idempotency_conflict. Kept 24 h. |

### `upload_asset`

**Upload an asset (base64)**. Scope: `write`. REST: `POST /v1/assets`.

Uploads a small file you already have (image incl. SVG, audio, video, font) as base64, for example a logo or generated audio. The type is checked from the bytes. With projectId it is added to the project as assetId. MCP messages are limited to a few MB; for larger files use REST POST /v1/assets (multipart) or add_asset_from_url. Use it in scenes by its manifest id: template props media: { asset, fit: cover\|contain\|blur-fill, start (video in-point, s), dim } and logo: { asset, corner, size }, or asset:<id> in html scenes (<img src="asset:logo">, <video src="asset:clip">, url(asset:hero)). Video is frame-accurate at any frame rate; SVG is stored sanitised (no scripts, handlers or remote references). A font is used by naming its family (metadata.font.family) in the theme fontFamily; Inter, Source Serif 4 and JetBrains Mono are bundled. With projectId the asset belongs to that project; without, every project of the workspace may use it.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dataBase64` | string | yes | File content, base64. |
| `filename` | string | no |  |
| `projectId` | string | no | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `assetId` | string | no | Id to use in the manifest, e.g. "logo". |
| `license` | object | no | Licence metadata for the asset (recommended; missing licences produce a warning). |

### `list_assets`

**List assets**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/assets`.

Lists assets: with projectId, all of that project's manifest entries (one page, nextCursor null); otherwise the server asset store. Returns one page, newest first: at most `limit` items (default 50, max 200) and `nextCursor`. When nextCursor is not null there are more: call again with the same arguments plus `cursor: nextCursor` until it is null. Without a cursor you get the first (newest) page only, not everything.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | no | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `limit` | integer | no | Page size: 1 to 200, default 50. |
| `cursor` | string | no | nextCursor from the previous page of this list (same filters), unchanged. Omit for the first page. |

### `get_asset`

**Get an asset**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/assets/:id`.

Metadata of an asset in the store: content type, media type, size, sha256, source, licence, provider metadata (e.g. TTS word timestamps).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `assetId` | string | yes | Store id, e.g. "ast-0123456789abcdef". |

### `set_audio`

**Set music, voice and sound effects**. Scope: `write`. REST: `PATCH /v1/projects/:id/audio`.

Merges into the project audio: { music: { asset, volume 0..1, fadeOutSeconds }, voice: { asset, volume, startFrame }, sfx: [{ asset, atFrame, volume }] }. Assets are project asset ids (add them with add_asset_from_url or generate_voice). Use null to remove music or voice. Every render has an AAC track (silence if no audio).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `audio` | object | yes |  |
| `expectedVersion` | integer | no | Optional optimistic-concurrency check: the project version you last read. The call fails with version_conflict if it changed. |

## Captions

Caption cues in one or more languages: imported from SRT or WebVTT, written by hand, built from the voice's word timestamps (TTS or local speech-to-text), reviewed and approved before the final render. Rendered when captions.mode (or the server default) is burned, sidecar or both.

### `import_captions`

**Import captions (SRT or WebVTT)**. Scope: `write`. REST: `POST /v1/projects/:id/captions/import`.

Parses an SRT or WebVTT file (content as text; format detected from the WEBVTT header unless given) into caption cues and stores them as the project's captions.cues, replacing any. Optionally sets captions.mode (off, burned, sidecar, both) and language. Cues are checked against the caption quality rules by validate_project (42 characters per line, 2 lines, 20 characters per second, 0.833-7 s, 2-frame gaps).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `content` | string | yes | The SRT or WebVTT file as text. |
| `format` | "srt" \| "vtt" | no |  |
| `mode` | "off" \| "burned" \| "sidecar" \| "both" | no |  |
| `language` | string | no | BCP 47 language tag, e.g. "en". |
| `expectedVersion` | integer | no | Optional optimistic-concurrency check: the project version you last read. The call fails with version_conflict if it changed. |

### `get_captions`

**Get captions for review**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/projects/:id/captions`, `GET /v1/renders/:id/captions`.

Returns the captions of a project (projectId) or of a finished render (renderId): for every language (BCP 47; the primary one first) the caption cues ({ start, end, text } in seconds, with word timings when known), the audio-description cues, which language is burned in, and the quality check (qa: characters per line, lines, reading speed, durations, gaps). For a project also the effective mode (and whether it comes from the project, the server default or nowhere), an etag and whether the user approved these captions. Before the final render, show the user the cue texts and times (and any qa issues) and ask whether to approve or change them; do not assume approval.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | no | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `renderId` | string | no | A render id: the captions as they were rendered. |
| `language` | string | no | Only this language. |

### `update_captions`

**Edit or approve captions**. Scope: `write`. REST: `PATCH /v1/projects/:id/captions`.

Edits the captions of a project with an optimistic-concurrency check: pass the etag from get_captions (refused with captions_conflict if anything changed since; read again and show the user the new state). Either replace every cue of one language (cues; a new language tag adds a language, [] removes it) or change some by their get_captions index (edits: { index, text?, start?, end?, delete? }, kind "description" for audio-description cues). Cues built from the voice are saved as manual cues when edited. Also sets mode (off, burned, sidecar, both), burnLanguage (the one language burned in) and highlight. approve: true records that the user approved the captions as they are after this call (only when the user said so); any later change voids it. Returns the same view as get_captions with the quality check re-run. Audit-logged.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `etag` | string | yes | etag from get_captions. |
| `language` | string | no | Language to edit; default the primary language. |
| `cues` | object[] | no | All cues of this language: { start, end, text, kind? ("description" for audio description) }. |
| `edits` | object[] | no |  |
| `mode` | "off" \| "burned" \| "sidecar" \| "both" | no |  |
| `burnLanguage` | string \| null | no | The language burned into the video; null: the primary language. |
| `highlight` | "none" \| "word" | no |  |
| `approve` | boolean | no | true only after the user approved these captions; false withdraws an approval. |
| `expectedVersion` | integer | no | Optional optimistic-concurrency check: the project version you last read. The call fails with version_conflict if it changed. |

### `transcribe_captions`

**Transcribe the voice-over (speech-to-text)**. Scope: `render`. REST: `POST /v1/projects/:id/captions/transcribe`.

Runs the server's local speech-to-text (faster-whisper, when installed: get_capabilities captions.stt.available) on the project's voice track and stores the word timings on it; caption cues are then built from them (like generate_voice timestamps). No network and no cost, but it takes CPU time (seconds to minutes) and one runs at a time (stt_busy: retry later). Upload the voice-over first (upload_asset with projectId, then set_audio { voice: { asset } }). language: "auto" (default from the server) or the spoken language. Manual caption cues take precedence: replaceCues: true removes them. Then get_captions and ask the user to review.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `language` | string | no | "auto" or a BCP 47 tag such as "en" or "pt-BR". |
| `provider` | string | no | Speech-to-text provider id; default from the server (captions.stt.provider). |
| `replaceCues` | boolean | no |  |
| `expectedVersion` | integer | no | Optional optimistic-concurrency check: the project version you last read. The call fails with version_conflict if it changed. |

## Media providers

Optional providers the operator configures with their own keys. Calls that cost money ask for acknowledgeCost.

### `list_providers`

**List media providers**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/providers`.

Media providers (TTS, ...) installed on this server, whether the operator configured them, and their cost notes.

No arguments.

### `configure_provider`

**Configure a media provider (owner)**. Scope: `owner`. REST: `PUT /v1/providers/:id/config`.

Sets or clears a provider setting such as ELEVENLABS_API_KEY (see list_providers for each provider's setting names). Values are stored encrypted in the server database (needs REELFORGE_SECRET_KEY on the server) and never returned; list_providers then shows set: true and source "api". Use null to clear a value (the environment variable, if any, applies again). Needs the owner scope (instance-level, #304). Only do this with a key the user gave you for this purpose.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `providerId` | string | yes |  |
| `values` | object | yes | Setting name -> value, or null to clear. |

### `run_provider`

**Run a media provider**. Scope: `render`. REST: `POST /v1/providers/:id/run`.

Runs any configured provider with its own parameters (see list_providers) and stores the result as an asset. May cost the operator money: without acknowledgeCost you get the cost note; ask the user first. For voice-overs generate_voice is simpler.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `providerId` | string | yes |  |
| `params` | object | yes |  |
| `projectId` | string | no | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `assetId` | string | no |  |
| `attachAs` | "voice" \| "none" | no |  |
| `acknowledgeCost` | boolean | no |  |
| `idempotencyKey` | string | no | Optional idempotency key (e.g. a UUID you generate once per intended action): retrying the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result instead of doing it twice; the same key with different arguments fails with idempotency_conflict. Kept 24 h. |

### `generate_voice`

**Generate a voice-over (TTS provider)**. Scope: `render`. REST: `POST /v1/providers/:id/run`.

Creates a voice-over audio asset with a configured TTS provider (e.g. "elevenlabs") and returns word timestamps. This can cost the operator money: the first call without acknowledgeCost returns the cost note; ask the user, then call again with acknowledgeCost: true. Identical requests are served from cache for free. With projectId, the audio is added as asset "voice" and set as the project voice track.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | string | no |  |
| `text` | string | yes |  |
| `voiceId` | string | yes | Provider voice id. |
| `modelId` | string | no |  |
| `projectId` | string | no | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `acknowledgeCost` | boolean | no |  |
| `idempotencyKey` | string | no | Optional idempotency key (e.g. a UUID you generate once per intended action): retrying the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result instead of doing it twice; the same key with different arguments fails with idempotency_conflict. Kept 24 h. |

## Rendering and jobs

Renders run as jobs: queued, running, then succeeded, failed or cancelled. get_analytics_summary aggregates them over a time range.

### `preview_scene`

**Render a quick preview**. Scope: `render`. REST: `POST /v1/projects/:id/preview`.

Starts a low-resolution preview render (default 1/3 size) of one scene, or of the whole project when sceneId is omitted; with variant, at that output variant's size and platform (the layout reflowed for it). Previews are queued at priority "interactive" (ahead of renders) by default. Returns a job; call get_job with waitSeconds: 45 until it finishes, then get_render_output (includes a poster image). When the server is busy it refuses with 429: too_many_jobs (your key has too many unfinished jobs), queue_full (the queue is full, or a new job would wait longer than limits.maxEstimatedWaitSeconds; details has the estimate and queued counts) or quota_exceeded. Wait details.retryAfterSeconds, then call again with the same idempotencyKey.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `sceneId` | string | no |  |
| `scale` | number | no |  |
| `variant` | string | no | Preview at this output variant (an id from the manifest's variants). Omit for output. |
| `priority` | "interactive" \| "standard" \| "batch" | no | Queue priority: jobs are started interactive first, then standard, then batch (fairly across API keys within a class). Default "interactive" for a preview. Use "batch" for work that can wait. A higher class than your key allows (get_capabilities limits.priority.maxForThisKey) is refused with priority_not_allowed. |
| `idempotencyKey` | string | no | Optional idempotency key (e.g. a UUID you generate once per intended action): retrying the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result instead of doing it twice; the same key with different arguments fails with idempotency_conflict. Kept 24 h. |

### `render_project`

**Render the project**. Scope: `render`. REST: `POST /v1/projects/:id/renders`.

Validates the project and starts the final render (every scene with its engine, assembled with audio, checked with ffprobe and a full decode). Returns a job immediately; renders take seconds to minutes. Renders are queued at priority "standard" by default. Then call get_job with waitSeconds: 45 (repeat while it is still running) until status is succeeded or failed, then call get_render_output. Several formats from one project: give the manifest variants, e.g. [{ id: "vertical", width: 1080, height: 1920 }, { id: "wide", width: 1920, height: 1080 }, { id: "square", width: 1080, height: 1080 }]; this call then starts one render per variant (each its own job and render id, the templates laid out again for each size) and answers { job, jobs, batchId }: wait for every job in jobs. Pass variant to render only one of them. When the server is busy it refuses with 429: too_many_jobs (your key has too many unfinished jobs), queue_full (the queue is full, or a new job would wait longer than limits.maxEstimatedWaitSeconds; details has the estimate and queued counts) or quota_exceeded. Wait details.retryAfterSeconds, then call again with the same idempotencyKey.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `backend` | string | no | Render backend id; default from the manifest ("local"). |
| `variant` | string | no | Render only this output variant (an id from the manifest's variants). Omit to render every variant, or output when the manifest has none. |
| `priority` | "interactive" \| "standard" \| "batch" | no | Queue priority: jobs are started interactive first, then standard, then batch (fairly across API keys within a class). Default "standard" for a render. Use "batch" for work that can wait. A higher class than your key allows (get_capabilities limits.priority.maxForThisKey) is refused with priority_not_allowed. |
| `captions` | "off" \| "burned" \| "sidecar" \| "both" | no | Captions for this render, overriding the manifest's captions.mode (and the server default captions.defaultMode): off, burned into the video, sidecar files (SRT, WebVTT, ASS per language) next to final.mp4, or both. |
| `audio` | object | no | Audio for this render, overriding the manifest: mute (silence everything), voice / music / sfx (false leaves that track out), loudness (social -14 LUFS, broadcast-ebu -23, broadcast-atsc -24, podcast -16, off). E.g. { music: false } for a voice-only cut, { mute: true } for a silent autoplay version. |
| `idempotencyKey` | string | no | Optional idempotency key (e.g. a UUID you generate once per intended action): retrying the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result instead of doing it twice; the same key with different arguments fails with idempotency_conflict. Kept 24 h. |

### `get_job`

**Get job status**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/jobs/:id`, `GET /v1/jobs/:id/events`.

Status of a render/preview job: queued, running (with progress stage and fraction), succeeded (result has renderId and output URLs), failed (error with code and stage) or cancelled. Renders take from seconds to several minutes: pass waitSeconds (up to 50) to wait for the job to finish instead of calling this repeatedly; it returns early as soon as the job finishes, otherwise the current progress.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `jobId` | string | yes |  |
| `waitSeconds` | integer | no | Wait up to this many seconds for the job to finish (0 = answer at once). Use 45 while a render runs. |

### `list_jobs`

**List jobs**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/jobs`.

Lists render and preview jobs, optionally only those of one project (projectId) and/or the units and the join of one fanned-out render (parentId: the render job's id; each unit renders one scene). To follow one job, call get_job with its id instead: a render's progress already covers its units. Returns one page, newest first: at most `limit` items (default 50, max 200) and `nextCursor`. When nextCursor is not null there are more: call again with the same arguments plus `cursor: nextCursor` until it is null. Without a cursor you get the first (newest) page only, not everything.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | no | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |
| `parentId` | string | no | Only the children of this job: the render_unit jobs and the render_join job of a fanned-out render (render.fanOut), given the render job's id. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Page size: 1 to 200, default 50. |
| `cursor` | string | no | nextCursor from the previous page of this list (same filters), unchanged. Omit for the first page. |

### `get_job_logs`

**Get job logs**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/jobs/:id/logs`.

Log lines of a job (use when a job failed to see the failing stage and tool output).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `jobId` | string | yes |  |
| `tail` | integer | no | Only the last N lines. |

### `cancel_job`

**Cancel a job**. Scope: `render`, destructive, idempotent. REST: `POST /v1/jobs/:id/cancel`.

Cancels a queued or running job. A cancelled render leaves no partial output and never touches earlier renders.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `jobId` | string | yes |  |

### `retry_job`

**Retry a failed or cancelled job**. Scope: `render`. REST: `POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry`.

Starts a new job with the same parameters as a failed or cancelled one (same project version). Earlier outputs are never overwritten.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `jobId` | string | yes |  |
| `idempotencyKey` | string | no | Optional idempotency key (e.g. a UUID you generate once per intended action): retrying the call with the same key and arguments returns the first result instead of doing it twice; the same key with different arguments fails with idempotency_conflict. Kept 24 h. |

### `get_render_output`

**Get a render output**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/renders/:id`, `GET /v1/renders/:id/output`.

Returns the output of a finished render: format, codec, alpha, file and contentType (final.mp4 by default; final.mov, final.webm, final.gif, frames.zip, final.m4a or final.wav for other output.format values), downloadUrl (a signed link to that file that works WITHOUT a key until downloadUrlExpiresAt, about 1 hour; give this to the user or to curl), outputUrl (same file, needs Authorization: Bearer), poster (not for audio-only) and render-manifest URLs, size, fps, frame count, duration, checks and tool versions. checks.freeze, checks.black and checks.flash are "warn" when the picture froze, went black or flashes more than three times a second (a seizure risk); videoQa.issues names the times and scenes: fix those scenes. Give renderId, or jobId of a succeeded job. includePoster (default true) attaches a small PNG so you can look at it: the first frame of an MP4, the middle frame of other formats (transparent where the render keeps alpha). To see every scene and cut, call get_frames.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `renderId` | string | no |  |
| `jobId` | string | no |  |
| `includePoster` | boolean | no |  |

### `get_frames`

**Look at frames of a render**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/renders/:id/frames`.

Stills of exact frames of a finished render or preview, so you can SEE what you made before calling it done: one labelled contact sheet (default) or one image per frame, taken from the stored file (no re-render). Default selection ("auto"): the first frame, the middle of every scene, both frames of every cut (last frame of a scene, first of the next) and the last frame, at most 24. Or at: times in seconds, { frame } indices or { sceneId, position: start\|mid\|end }; or everySeconds. Each tile is labelled scene · position · frame · time, and the JSON lists the same. overlay "safe" tints what lies outside the safe area for the render's size and platform (text there is covered by the app or cut off). width is the tile width (default 360, the width of a phone; 120 to 720). Use it after preview_scene and before render_project, and on every final render: fix what you see, preview again. Give renderId, or jobId of a succeeded job.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `renderId` | string | no |  |
| `jobId` | string | no |  |
| `at` | (number \| object)[] | no | Frames to show instead of the automatic selection. |
| `everySeconds` | number | no | One frame every N seconds from 0 (at most 24 frames). |
| `width` | integer | no | Tile width in pixels (default 360). |
| `layout` | "sheet" \| "separate" | no | sheet (default): one image; separate: one image per frame. |
| `overlay` | "none" \| "safe" | no | safe: tint what lies outside the safe area (default none). The video is never changed. |

### `list_renders`

**List renders of a project**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/projects/:id/renders`.

Lists finished renders and previews of a project, newest first, with output URLs, size, fps, frames and duration.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | yes | Project id (the manifest's projectId). |

### `get_analytics_summary`

**Get render analytics**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/analytics/summary`.

Aggregates for a time range (default: the last 30 days by UTC day; at most 90 days, or 7 days with bucket "hour"): render and preview jobs per bucket by status (succeeded, failed, cancelled, unfinished), success and failure rates (failed / (succeeded + failed); cancelled jobs are left out), render time and queue wait (p50 and p95 in ms), scene render time per engine (p50, p95, from the manifests of the newest 200 successful renders), minutes rendered, storage used (measured at most every 5 minutes), the top error codes of failed jobs, and webhook deliveries per status and endpoint. scan.truncated says when the range had more jobs than one call reads (20 000); the figures then cover scan.coveredFrom to range.to. Needs the read scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | no | Start: ISO 8601 time or a UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD). Aligned down to the bucket. Default: 29 days before today (UTC), or 24 hours before `to` with bucket "hour". |
| `to` | string | no | End, exclusive: ISO 8601 time, or a UTC date (that whole day is included). Default: now. |
| `bucket` | "day" \| "hour" | no | Bucket size of the series (default day). |

## Workspaces

Every key belongs to one workspace and sees only its projects, assets, themes, jobs, renders, keys, webhooks and audit log (#304, docs/WORKSPACES.md). Managing workspaces needs the instance-level owner scope.

### `get_workspace`

**Get this key's workspace**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/workspace`.

The workspace this API key belongs to (#304): id, name, status, the limits in force (renders per day/month, requests per minute, storage bytes; absent: unlimited) and its usage today, this month and in storage. Every project, asset, theme, job, render, key, webhook and audit entry you can see is in this workspace only.

No arguments.

### `list_workspaces`

**List workspaces (owner)**. Scope: `owner`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/workspaces`.

Every workspace of this install with its status (active, suspended, deleted with purgeAfter), its own limits and the limits in force. Needs the owner scope (instance-level, #304).

No arguments.

### `create_workspace`

**Create a workspace (owner)**. Scope: `owner`. REST: `POST /v1/workspaces`.

Creates a workspace for a team or customer: its projects, assets, themes, jobs, renders, keys, webhooks and audit log are invisible to every other workspace. id: 1-40 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Optional limits (renders per day/month, requests per minute, storage bytes; default unlimited). adminKey: true (or { name, scopes }) also creates the workspace's first admin key and returns it ONCE: give it to the user. Needs the owner scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `name` | string | no |  |
| `limits` | object | no | rendersPerDay, rendersPerMonth, rateLimitPerMinute, storageBytes; 0 or null: unlimited. |
| `adminKey` | boolean \| object | no |  |

### `update_workspace`

**Rename, limit, suspend or resume a workspace (owner)**. Scope: `owner`, idempotent. REST: `PATCH /v1/workspaces/:id`.

Changes a workspace's name or limits (null clears them: the workspaces.* defaults apply), or suspends it (suspended: true: its keys are refused with workspace_suspended and its queued jobs wait; its data stays) and resumes it (false). The default workspace cannot be suspended. Confirm suspending with the user first. Needs the owner scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | string | yes |  |
| `name` | string | no |  |
| `limits` | object \| null | no |  |
| `suspended` | boolean | no |  |

### `delete_workspace`

**Delete a workspace (owner)**. Scope: `owner`, destructive. REST: `DELETE /v1/workspaces/:id`.

Deletes a workspace: its keys stop working and its jobs are no longer run at once; its projects, renders, assets, keys, webhooks and audit log are purged for good after workspaces.deleteGraceDays (default 30; purgeAfter says when). restore_workspace undoes it until then. The default workspace cannot be deleted. Confirm with the user first. Needs the owner scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | string | yes |  |

### `restore_workspace`

**Restore a deleted workspace (owner)**. Scope: `owner`, idempotent. REST: `POST /v1/workspaces/:id/restore`.

Brings back a deleted workspace before its purge (see list_workspaces: purgeAfter): its keys work again and its jobs run. Needs the owner scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | string | yes |  |

## Licence

Renders need an activated licence key. Everything else works without one.

### `get_licence`

**Get the licence status**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/licence`.

Returns the licence status of this server: status "valid" (full use), "grace" (the licence server is unreachable; renders keep working until graceUntil), "invalid" (renders and previews are refused; reason, message and fix say why and what to do), "unlicensed" (no key) or "checking". Also: renderAllowed, last check and last success, item, activations used/limit, the key masked (first group only). Reading, listing and downloading always work. If renders are refused, tell the user the message and fix; activating needs the admin scope.

No arguments.

### `activate_licence`

**Set and activate the licence key (owner)**. Scope: `owner`, idempotent. REST: `POST /v1/licence`.

Stores the licence key (encrypted; needs REELFORGE_SECRET_KEY on the server) and activates it for this server with the licence server, then returns the status (see get_licence). Without key, the configured key is activated or checked again (e.g. after a network outage or deactivate_licence). Only the key and a random instance id are sent. Only do this with a key the user gave you. Needs the owner scope (instance-level, #304).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | no | The licence key from the RenderWeld purchase, e.g. "ABCDE-FGHJK-LMNPQ-RSTUV-WXYZ2". Omit to re-check the configured key. |

### `deactivate_licence`

**Give the licence activation back (owner)**. Scope: `owner`, destructive. REST: `DELETE /v1/licence`.

Frees this server's activation of the licence key at the licence server, so the key can be activated on another server. Afterwards renders and previews are refused here until activate_licence is called again. Only do this when the user asks (e.g. moving to a new server). Needs the owner scope (instance-level, #304).

No arguments.

## Administration

Configuration, storage, API keys and the audit log. These need a key with the admin scope.

### `get_config`

**Get the server configuration (owner)**. Scope: `owner`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/config`.

Returns every server setting with its effective value and where it comes from: source "default", "file" (REELFORGE_CONFIG), "env" (origin names the variable) or "runtime" (set with update_config, stored in the database; wins over the others). scope "runtime" settings can be changed with update_config; scope "startup" ones only in the config file or environment, then a restart. Secrets are only "set" / "not set". Optional prefix filters keys, e.g. "limits". Needs the owner scope (instance-level, #304).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prefix` | string | no | Only keys under this group, e.g. "limits" or "providers.elevenlabs". |

### `update_config`

**Change runtime settings (owner)**. Scope: `owner`. REST: `PATCH /v1/config`.

Changes runtime settings at once and stores them in the database (they survive restarts and override the config file and environment). settings maps dotted keys from get_config to values, e.g. { "limits.rateLimitPerMinute": 120 }; null clears a runtime value (the file/env/default applies again). All or nothing: start-up-only keys (port, database URL, data directory, ...) are refused with where to set them. Secrets (provider keys, licence key) are stored encrypted and need REELFORGE_SECRET_KEY on the server. Every change is audit-logged. Needs the owner scope (instance-level, #304). Only change what the user asked for.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `settings` | object | yes | Dotted setting key -> new value (JSON type of the setting), or null to clear the runtime value. |

### `get_storage`

**Get storage driver, usage and health (owner)**. Scope: `owner`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/storage`.

Returns where asset and render files are stored: driver ("local", "s3", "azure", "gcs"), location (bucket/container, endpoint, prefix, credential source; never secrets), how download links are made (bucket-signed or through this server), health (can the store be reached), usage (assets, renders, unfinished uploads, local cache in objects and bytes), the retention policy (storage.retention.*, change it with update_config) and the last scheduled sweep. Needs the owner scope (instance-level, #304).

No arguments.

### `run_storage_cleanup`

**Apply the storage retention policy now (owner)**. Scope: `owner`, destructive. REST: `POST /v1/storage/cleanup`.

Deletes renders the retention policy no longer keeps (older than storage.retention.renderDays; the newest keepLastRendersPerProject of each project and renders of running jobs are always kept), unfinished uploads and stale staging directories older than tempHours, and local cached copies unused for cacheDays. Call with dryRun: true first and show the user what would be deleted; deleting renders cannot be undone. renderDays / keepLastRendersPerProject try another policy for this run only (to set the policy, use update_config). Returns every render removed with its size and reason. Audit-logged. Needs the owner scope (instance-level, #304).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dryRun` | boolean | no | true: only report what would be deleted. Default false. |
| `renderDays` | integer | no | Override storage.retention.renderDays for this run (0 = no age limit). |
| `keepLastRendersPerProject` | integer | no | Override storage.retention.keepLastRendersPerProject for this run. |

### `list_keys`

**List API keys (admin)**. Scope: `admin`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/keys`.

Lists API keys: id, name, scopes, prefix, status (active, expired, revoked), created, last used, expiry, limits, quotas, IP allowlist and, after a rotation, until when the old secret works. Never returns secrets. Needs the admin scope.

No arguments.

### `get_key`

**Get an API key (admin)**. Scope: `admin`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/keys/:id`.

One API key (as list_keys shows it) with its render usage today and this month (UTC). Never returns the secret. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keyId` | string | yes |  |

### `create_key`

**Create an API key (admin)**. Scope: `admin`. REST: `POST /v1/keys`.

Creates an API key in this key's workspace with the given scopes (read, write, render, admin; owner only from an owner key) and optional expiry, per-key rate limit, render quotas (per UTC day / month) and IP allowlist (CIDR). The key is returned once: give it to the user, never store it elsewhere. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `scopes` | ("read" \| "write" \| "render" \| "admin")[] | yes |  |
| `expiresAt` | string \| null | no | ISO-8601 time the key stops working, e.g. "2027-01-31T00:00:00Z"; null: never. |
| `expiresInDays` | number | no | Shortcut for expiresAt: this many days from now. |
| `rateLimitPerMinute` | integer \| null | no | Requests per minute for this key (null: the server default; 0: no limit). |
| `rendersPerDay` | integer \| null | no | Render and preview jobs per UTC day (null: unlimited). |
| `rendersPerMonth` | integer \| null | no | Render and preview jobs per calendar month, UTC (null: unlimited). |
| `ipAllowlist` | string[] \| null | no | CIDR blocks the key may be used from, e.g. ["203.0.113.0/24"]; null or []: anywhere. |
| `maxPriority` | "interactive" \| "standard" \| "batch" \| null | no | Highest job priority the key may ask for: "interactive" lets it start renders ahead of other renders; "batch" keeps all its jobs behind everyone else's. null: each job type's default (previews interactive, renders standard), so the key can lower a job's priority but not raise it. |

### `update_key`

**Change an API key (admin)**. Scope: `admin`, idempotent. REST: `PATCH /v1/keys/:id`.

Changes a key's name, expiry, rate limit, render quotas or IP allowlist (null clears one). Scopes cannot change: create a new key. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keyId` | string | yes |  |
| `name` | string | no |  |
| `expiresAt` | string \| null | no | ISO-8601 time the key stops working, e.g. "2027-01-31T00:00:00Z"; null: never. |
| `expiresInDays` | number | no | Shortcut for expiresAt: this many days from now. |
| `rateLimitPerMinute` | integer \| null | no | Requests per minute for this key (null: the server default; 0: no limit). |
| `rendersPerDay` | integer \| null | no | Render and preview jobs per UTC day (null: unlimited). |
| `rendersPerMonth` | integer \| null | no | Render and preview jobs per calendar month, UTC (null: unlimited). |
| `ipAllowlist` | string[] \| null | no | CIDR blocks the key may be used from, e.g. ["203.0.113.0/24"]; null or []: anywhere. |
| `maxPriority` | "interactive" \| "standard" \| "batch" \| null | no | Highest job priority the key may ask for: "interactive" lets it start renders ahead of other renders; "batch" keeps all its jobs behind everyone else's. null: each job type's default (previews interactive, renders standard), so the key can lower a job's priority but not raise it. |

### `rotate_key`

**Rotate an API key (admin)**. Scope: `admin`. REST: `POST /v1/keys/:id/rotate`.

Gives a key a new secret (returned once) and keeps the old secret working for graceHours (default: the server setting keys.rotationGraceHours, 24 h), so clients can switch without downtime. Same id, name, scopes and limits. You may rotate the key you are using. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keyId` | string | yes |  |
| `graceHours` | number | no | Hours the old secret keeps working (0: stops at once). |

### `revoke_key`

**Revoke an API key (admin)**. Scope: `admin`, destructive, idempotent. REST: `POST /v1/keys/:id/revoke`.

Revokes a key: it (and any old secret still in its rotation grace window) stops working at once. The key stays listed with status "revoked" so the audit trail still names it. You cannot revoke the key you are using. Confirm with the user first. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keyId` | string | yes |  |

### `delete_key`

**Delete an API key (admin)**. Scope: `admin`, destructive. REST: `DELETE /v1/keys/:id`.

Deletes an API key; it stops working immediately and disappears from list_keys (prefer revoke_key, which keeps it listed for the audit trail). You cannot delete the key you are using. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keyId` | string | yes |  |

### `list_audit_events`

**Read the audit log (admin)**. Scope: `admin`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/audit`.

The audit trail, newest first: who (API key id and name), action (e.g. "key.rotate", "project.create", "config.update"), target, result (success, failure, denied), client IP, user agent, request id and time (UTC), of this key's workspace (owner keys: any workspace with workspaceId). Never contains secret values. Filter by time (from/to), actorId, action ("key.*" for a prefix), targetType/targetId and result; page with cursor (nextCursor). format "jsonl" or "csv" returns an export (up to 10 000 entries; the REST route GET /v1/audit?format= streams up to 100 000). Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | no | Entries at or after this ISO time. |
| `to` | string | no | Entries before this ISO time. |
| `actorId` | string | no | Only this actor (API key id). |
| `action` | string | no | Exact action ("key.rotate") or a prefix with * ("key.*"). |
| `targetType` | string | no | e.g. "key", "project", "config". |
| `targetId` | string | no |  |
| `result` | "success" \| "failure" \| "denied" | no |  |
| `limit` | integer | no | Page size (default 100, max 1000) or export size (max 10 000). |
| `cursor` | string | no | nextCursor of the previous page. |
| `format` | "json" \| "jsonl" \| "csv" | no | json (default): a page of entries; jsonl / csv: an export as text. |
| `workspaceId` | string | no | Owner keys only: another workspace's trail, or "*" for every workspace merged newest first (json pages; each entry then names its workspaceId). |

## Webhooks and notifications

Signed webhook endpoints (Standard Webhooks), terminal render events, their delivery log, resends and secret rotation. Admin scope, except get_webhook_log (read). Notification channels (Slack, Discord, Teams, email) are configured with update_config.

### `list_webhooks`

**List webhooks and notification channels (admin)**. Scope: `admin`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/webhooks`.

Lists outbound event endpoints: signed webhooks (Standard Webhooks), Slack, Discord and Microsoft Teams incoming webhooks, and email channels (SMTP, Resend, Postmark, Amazon SES, SendGrid), with the events each one receives, whether it is enabled, and whether its provider is configured. URLs are masked; signing secrets are never returned. Also lists every event type. Needs the admin scope.

No arguments.

### `get_webhook`

**Get a webhook (admin)**. Scope: `admin`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/webhooks/:id`.

One endpoint as list_webhooks shows it, with its delivery counts (pending, delivering, succeeded, dead). Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `webhookId` | string | yes |  |

### `create_webhook`

**Create a webhook or notification channel (admin)**. Scope: `admin`. REST: `POST /v1/webhooks`.

Sends server events to an endpoint so automations (n8n, Zapier, Make, your backend) or people react without polling. type "webhook" (default): an HTTPS POST of {id, type, timestamp, data} signed per Standard Webhooks (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature "v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256>"); the signing secret (whsec_...) is returned ONCE: give it to the user to verify signatures. type "slack" / "discord" / "teams": the channel's incoming webhook URL. type "email": email { provider: smtp\|resend\|postmark\|ses\|sendgrid, to: [addresses] } (the provider is set up with update_config, notifications.email.*). events: event types or patterns: job.queued, job.started, job.progress, job.succeeded, job.failed, job.cancelled, render.ready, render.failed, render.cancelled, render.timeout, render.qa_failed, render.blocked (one terminal render.* event per render job), licence.state_changed, key.created, key.revoked, config.changed, audit.entry, "job.*", "render.*", or "*" (all but job.progress and audit.entry). Deliveries are retried with exponential backoff for up to 24 h (10 s timeout per attempt), then marked dead. Private and http:// URLs are refused unless the operator allowed them at start-up. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | A label, e.g. "n8n render pipeline". |
| `type` | "webhook" \| "slack" \| "discord" \| "teams" \| "email" | no | Default "webhook". |
| `url` | string | no | https:// URL (webhook, slack, discord, teams). |
| `email` | object | no | Email channels only. |
| `events` | string[] | yes | Event types or patterns, e.g. ["render.ready", "job.failed"]. |
| `description` | string | no |  |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Default true. |

### `update_webhook`

**Change a webhook (admin)**. Scope: `admin`. REST: `PATCH /v1/webhooks/:id`.

Changes an endpoint's name, description, url, email recipients, events or enabled flag (enabling clears a "disabled by the server" reason, e.g. after a 410 Gone). rotateSecret: true gives a webhook a new signing secret (returned once); for graceHours (default webhooks.secretRotationGraceHours, 24) every message carries signatures with the new and the old secret, so the receiver can switch without missing messages. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `webhookId` | string | yes |  |
| `name` | string | no |  |
| `description` | string \| null | no |  |
| `url` | string | no |  |
| `email` | object | no |  |
| `events` | string[] | no |  |
| `enabled` | boolean | no |  |
| `rotateSecret` | boolean | no |  |
| `graceHours` | number | no | With rotateSecret: hours the old secret keeps signing (0: stops at once). |

### `delete_webhook`

**Delete a webhook (admin)**. Scope: `admin`, destructive. REST: `DELETE /v1/webhooks/:id`.

Deletes an endpoint; its pending deliveries are abandoned (kept in the delivery log as dead). Confirm with the user first. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `webhookId` | string | yes |  |

### `test_webhook`

**Send a test event (admin)**. Scope: `admin`. REST: `POST /v1/webhooks/:id/test`.

Sends a "webhook.test" event to one endpoint through the normal outbox (signed, retried). With waitSeconds (up to 30) it waits for the first attempt and returns its outcome (HTTP status or error), so you can tell the user whether the receiver works. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `webhookId` | string | yes |  |
| `waitSeconds` | number | no | Wait for the first attempt (default 0: return at once). |

### `list_webhook_deliveries`

**Read the delivery log (admin)**. Scope: `admin`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/webhooks/:id/deliveries`.

Deliveries of one endpoint, newest first: event type, webhook-id (messageId), status (pending, delivering, succeeded, dead), attempts, next attempt, last HTTP status and error, and the attempt log (time, duration, status, outcome). Filter by status (e.g. "dead" for the dead letter queue) or eventType; page with cursor (nextCursor). includePayload: true adds the event payload. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `webhookId` | string | yes |  |
| `status` | "pending" \| "delivering" \| "succeeded" \| "dead" | no |  |
| `eventType` | string | no |  |
| `limit` | integer | no | Default 50. |
| `cursor` | string | no | nextCursor of the previous page. |
| `includePayload` | boolean | no |  |
| `includeAttempts` | boolean | no | Default true. |

### `replay_webhook_delivery`

**Send a delivery again (admin)**. Scope: `admin`. REST: `POST /v1/webhooks/:id/deliveries/:deliveryId/replay`.

Sends a finished delivery (dead or succeeded) again: a new outbox entry with the same payload and the same webhook-id, so receivers that already processed it can ignore it. Use it after fixing a receiver that was down. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `webhookId` | string | yes |  |
| `deliveryId` | string | yes |  |

### `resend_webhook`

**Send an event to a webhook again (admin)**. Scope: `admin`. REST: `POST /v1/webhooks/:id/resend`.

Sends one event to an endpoint again, named by exactly one of: deliveryId (from get_webhook_log), eventId, or dedupeKey ("render:<jobId>": the terminal outcome of a render job). A delivery still waiting for its next retry is sent now ("rescheduled"); a finished one (succeeded or dead) is queued again with the same payload and webhook-id ("queued", with a fresh 24 h retry window); an event the endpoint never got (found at another endpoint) is queued for it. Receivers deduplicate on webhook-id. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `webhookId` | string | yes |  |
| `deliveryId` | string | no |  |
| `eventId` | string | no |  |
| `dedupeKey` | string | no | e.g. "render:job_..." for the render.* outcome of that job. |

### `rotate_webhook_secret`

**Rotate a webhook signing secret (admin)**. Scope: `admin`. REST: `POST /v1/webhooks/:id/rotate-secret`.

Gives a webhook a new signing secret (returned once; or bring your own with secret: "whsec_..."). For overlapHours (default webhooks.secretRotationGraceHours, 24) every message is signed with the new and the previous secret (two v1 signatures in webhook-signature), so the receiver accepts both while it switches. endOverlap: true stops signing with the previous secret at once. Needs the admin scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `webhookId` | string | yes |  |
| `overlapHours` | number | no | Hours both secrets sign (0: only the new one at once). |
| `secret` | string | no | Your own new secret: whsec_ + base64 of 24 to 64 bytes. Omit to get a generated one. |
| `endOverlap` | boolean | no | End the current overlap now (the receiver has switched). |

### `get_webhook_log`

**Read a webhook delivery log**. Scope: `read`, read-only. REST: `GET /v1/webhooks/:id/log`.

The delivery log of one endpoint, newest first, without payloads or the target URL: per delivery its event type, webhook-id, dedupeKey, status (pending, delivering, succeeded, dead = failed for good), attempts, latency (latencyMs of the last attempt, durationMs of each), last HTTP status and error, and giveUpAt while it is retried; a summary (success rate, p50/p95 latency) and the retry policy. Filter by status or eventType; page with cursor. Needs the read scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `webhookId` | string | yes |  |
| `status` | "pending" \| "delivering" \| "succeeded" \| "dead" | no |  |
| `eventType` | string | no |  |
| `limit` | integer | no | Default 50. |
| `cursor` | string | no | nextCursor of the previous page. |
